name: Monterado Castle

description:
Monterado's origin as a settlement on a characteristic Marche hill dates to July 13, 1267. It was originally built as a fortified village with defensive walls, became part of the Duchy of Urbino thanks to its strategic position overlooking the valley and the sea, and was taken by the Della Rovere during the Renaissance.

In 1742 the village passed to the Jesuits of the Collegium Germanicum et Hungaricum, who decided to completely transform the village's original appearance, incorporating the old defensive walls and using the entire area — houses and streets — of the small village to build a large, imposing palazzo. Prince Maximilian of Beauharnais, nephew of Josephine Bonaparte, chose to spend his honeymoon here after marrying the daughter of Tsar Alexander of Russia, and had the palazzo's interior richly decorated.

The Jesuits' 1742 decision to absorb an entire existing village — not just build alongside it — into a single unified palazzo is an unusually radical architectural transformation, distinct from the more common pattern of a castle simply expanding or being remodeled over time.

Prince Maximilian of Beauharnais's honeymoon connects Monterado to the broader web of Napoleonic-era dynastic marriages, linking a Bonaparte relative by marriage to the Russian imperial family within this Marche palazzo's own history.

The 19th-century frescoes by Corrado Corradi, present in nearly every room, give Monterado a level of coordinated interior decoration unusual even among the more elaborate castle-hotels in this collection.

The nearby Adriatic coast at Senigallia and the Riviera del Conero give guests staying at Monterado easy access to both beach tourism and the Marche's coastal landscape.
history: Monterado originated as a fortified hilltop village in 1267, becoming part of the Duchy of Urbino before being taken by the Della Rovere during the Renaissance. In 1742 the Jesuits of the Collegium Germanicum et Hungaricum absorbed the entire village into a single large palazzo. Prince Maximilian of Beauharnais, nephew of Josephine Bonaparte, honeymooned here after marrying Tsar Alexander of Russia's daughter. Today the palazzo's 15 rooms and 4 suites, many with 19th-century frescoes by Corrado Corradi, operate as a hotel, open since 2005.

faqs.question: Was Monterado Castle built over an existing village?
faqs.answer: Yes — in 1742 the Jesuits of the Collegium Germanicum et Hungaricum absorbed the entire original village, houses and streets included, into a single large palazzo, rather than building a separate new structure.

faqs.question: Who was Prince Maximilian of Beauharnais and what is his connection to Monterado?
faqs.answer: A nephew of Josephine Bonaparte who honeymooned at Monterado after marrying the daughter of Tsar Alexander of Russia, and who commissioned rich interior decoration for the palazzo.

faqs.question: Since when has Monterado Castle operated as a hotel?
faqs.answer: Since 2005 — before that it was a private residence.

hotel.how_to_stay:
**Getting there:** About 20 minutes from Senigallia and 40 minutes from Ancona by car; Ancona-Falconara Airport (AOI) is about 30 minutes away.

**Rooms & rates:** 15 rooms and 4 suites, many with 19th-century frescoes by Corrado Corradi, all within the large palazzo. From €133/night.

**On-site:** A 2-hectare English-style park with views over the Marche hills and the Adriatic Sea.

**Good to know:** Open as a hotel since 2005 (previously a private residence) — it retains an intimate character despite its palatial history.

**Combine with:** Senigallia and its "velvet beach" (~20 min), Ancona (~40 min), and the Riviera del Conero.
